newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Inflation is Portugal's main worry, OECD says.
newsitem.headline: Inflation is Portugal's main worry, OECD says.

text.p: Portugal should be able to sustain a budget deficit below single currency limits but inflation remains a potential concern, the OECD said in a report on Thursday.

The Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said that any let up in the fight against inflation could in turn halt the descent of long-term interest rates and eventually threaten budgetary targets.
Persistenly strong increases for non-tradeable goods prices, mainly wages, could slow the pace of disinflation and brake the decline in interest rates, it warned.

But providing there was no loss of market confidence in the government's commitment to fiscal consolidation and price restraint, then lower interest rates would compensate for projected higher primary spending and a decline in current revenues relative to gross domestic product (GDP).
"The budget deficit should thus stabilise at under three percent of GDP," the OECD said, referring to the ceiling for access to the European Union's planned Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

The OECD predicted that Portugal's budget deficit would narrow to 3.8 percent of GDP in 1996, below the government's 4.0 percent target, providing a good launching pad for reaching the 1997 EMU goal of 2.9 percent.
The single currency will be launched in January 1999 by countries which succeed next year in meeting a series of tough economic entry tests, including on the budget deficit.
The OECD said it expected economic growth to quicken to around 3.2 percent in 1997 from some 2.5 percent this year.
But unemployment would remain relatively high at 6.9 percent of the workforce in 1998 and this could help curb wage growth and push inflation to below 2.5 percent in 1998.
